source_title: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch signals IPO readiness as AI agents fuel revenue surge
claim_summary: Reporter cites third-party revenue estimates (about $100M ARR early 2024 per The Information; $340M run rate end Feb 2026 per Forbes); CEO says 30% of apps on the platform already come from agents and gives no IPO quarter
feature: company scale and agent-generated deployment share
limitation: Revenue numbers are secondhand media figures, not filings; the 30% agent share is an onstage CEO claim with no method; IPO is not announced; press is not adoption evidence

source_title: A new programming model for durable execution
claim_summary: Vendor states Vercel Workflows is generally available after an Oct 2025 beta; open-source Workflow SDK with use workflow/use step directives; Python SDK beta; Workflows 5 previewed via workflow@beta; self-hosted Postgres world adapter
availability: GA (TypeScript); Python SDK beta; v5 preview
limitation: Usage figures (100M+ runs; 1,500+ customers; 200K weekly npm downloads) are vendor-reported; npm downloads are not verified reuse; repo license Apache-2.0 per GitHub API 2026-10-16

source_title: Vercel April 2026 security incident
claim_summary: Bulletin (update log from Apr 19 to Apr 24) says the attack began with compromise of the third-party AI tool Context.ai used by an employee; the attacker took over Google Workspace then Vercel accounts and decrypted non-sensitive environment variables for a limited set of customers; vendor says its npm packages were not compromised
feature: secret handling; third-party AI tool OAuth risk
availability: incident disclosure; remediation advice and product enhancements reported
limitation: Bulletin shows no original publication timestamp, only an update log; affected-customer count undisclosed; threat-actor sale claims reported by CyberInsider are unverified; customer-side check by Trunk (Apr 20) reported no evidence of unauthorized access in its own logs

source_title: Introducing deepsec: The security harness for finding vulnerabilities in your codebase
claim_summary: Vendor open-sources a security harness that drives claude and codex coding agents through scan/investigate/revalidate/enrich/export, optionally fanned out to Vercel Sandboxes
limitation: Authors self-report about 10-20% false positives and multi-day scans on one machine; testimonials are anecdotal; repo license Apache-2.0 per GitHub API; no independent recall/precision benchmark

source_title: Next.js security advisories published 2026-05-06/07 (GHSA-267c-6grr-h53f and related)
claim_summary: GitHub advisory list shows 12 Next.js advisories published May 6 (including middleware/proxy bypasses, SSRF via WebSocket upgrades, XSS, cache poisoning, DoS) plus incomplete-fix follow-up GHSA-26hh-7cqf-hhc6 on May 7
limitation: Advisory count read from GitHub API; individual affected/fixed ranges must be checked per advisory; advisories describe potential impact not observed exploitation

source_title: AI Gateway production index
claim_summary: Vendor reports anonymized aggregate routing data from 200K+ teams through April 2026: tool-call requests 22.2% of requests and 58.9% of tokens (up from 11.4%/31.6% in Oct 2025); fallback completed about 3.5% of requests
limitation: Single-gateway sample, list-price spend, undisclosed classification method; not market share or task-outcome evidence

source_title: Protecting against token theft
claim_summary: Vendor describes an Apr 12 inference-theft surge (about 10x normal; peak 1,300 req/min) on its docs AI chat endpoint and says BotID deep analysis blocked over 10,000 bot requests; recommends per-request verification on AI endpoints
availability: BotID existing product; no new GA date stated
limitation: Single self-reported incident; no false-block rate or independent replication; BotID relies on a third-party (Kasada) per post

product: Vercel for Enterprise Apps and Agents
source_title: Vercel for Enterprise Apps and Agents
claim_summary: Vendor announces internal-app/agent governance bundle: Passport (beta) behind company IdP; Connect (beta); Enterprise Managed Users and BYOC on AWS (private beta); v0 with Snowflake
limitation: Mixed availability labels; Ship recap (Jun 30) lists Passport as public beta; no independent deployment evidence

source_title: Introducing Vercel Connect
claim_summary: Runtime credential exchange: apps authenticate with per-deployment OIDC and receive short-lived task-scoped provider tokens (e.g. one GitHub repo read-only) instead of storing secrets; trigger forwarding beta for Slack/GitHub/Linear
availability: public beta at publication; page note says GA 2026-08-25
limitation: Revocation, token lifetime and scope granularity depend on each provider; page was edited after publication (GA note)

source_title: Introducing eve
claim_summary: Open-source agent framework where an agent is a directory of files; durable workflow per conversation; isolated sandbox per agent (Vercel Sandbox or Docker/local); human approval steps; brokered MCP/OpenAPI credentials; OpenTelemetry and evals
limitation: Vendor claims 100+ internal production agents; other deploy targets only 'on the way'; repo Apache-2.0 per GitHub API (created 2026-06-16)

source_title: AI SDK 7
claim_summary: Major release adds tool approvals (optional HMAC-signed), durable WorkflowAgent, SandboxSession, MCP Apps, terminal UI, telemetry changes; experimental HarnessAgent to run Claude Code/Codex/Pi, realtime voice and video generation; codemod migration
limitation: Breaking changes not enumerated in post; migration cost unmeasured; repo LICENSE Apache-2.0 (GitHub API reports NOASSERTION; file read)

source_title: Vercel Services: Run full stack on Vercel
claim_summary: Multiple frameworks (e.g. Next.js frontend and FastAPI backend) declared under services in vercel.json deploy and roll back together and call each other over an internal network via bindings
limitation: Same-day Ship recap says Guillermo announced Services 'available July 1' (the words 'coming soon' do not appear in the recap as read 2026-10-16); availability date therefore ambiguous; lock-in/portability not assessed

source_title: Vercel acquires Better Auth to accelerate open source auth
claim_summary: Vercel acquires the company behind the Better Auth TypeScript auth library; team joins; library stays MIT with same governance; Agent Auth (scoped revocable agent identity) to be brought to Vercel Connect and eve
feature: OSS auth library stewardship; agent identity
limitation: 4.7M weekly npm downloads and 850 contributors are vendor figures; future license/governance continuity is a promise; repo LICENSE MIT per GitHub API 2026-10-16

source_title: Introducing the new Vercel Agent
claim_summary: Dashboard agent reviews PRs, investigates incidents, diagnoses builds and proposes fixes; runs as its own read-only identity by default; requests plan-scoped access; generated code runs in Vercel Sandbox; vendor says it never changes production on its own
availability: Pro and Enterprise teams; beta/GA label not stated (Jun 30 recap: public beta)
limitation: Only metric is one anecdotal under-three-minute mitigation; pricing unstated; no independent accuracy data

source_title: Next.js security advisories published 2026-07-21 (9 advisories incl. GHSA-6gpp-xcg3-4w24)
claim_summary: Nine advisories published Jul 21: middleware/proxy bypass with Turbopack single locale, two SSRF issues, Server Actions DoS, cache confusion, unbounded Edge payloads, SVG image DoS, endpoint disclosure
limitation: Count read from GitHub API; per-advisory ranges unverified here; no exploitation data

source_title: Next.js 16.3
claim_summary: Release with Instant Navigations (opt-in), Turbopack dev memory eviction (vendor: up to 90% less RAM), build disk cache, TypeScript 7 type-check, version-matched AGENTS.md block pointing coding agents to bundled docs (retiring earlier docs-only Skills)
limitation: Performance figures are vendor benchmarks on vendor apps; AGENTS.md effect on agent task success not independently tested

source_title: Introducing the new v0 API
claim_summary: New v0 API generally available: prompt-to-app generation in a Vercel Sandbox with preview URL, follow-up edits, chats from repo/ZIP/files, one-call deploy to a Vercel project, MCP server and AI SDK tools
limitation: Old-API chats must be migrated; no general code export described beyond ZIP; 'verifies the code' claim not independently tested; pricing not stated

source_title: Introducing Agent Plugins
claim_summary: Vercel-initiated vendor-neutral plugin manifest (plugin.json) packaging Agent Skills and MCP servers; launch clients ChatGPT/Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, VS Code; TSC maintainers from AWS, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, Vercel
limitation: Repo LICENSE.md: CC-BY-4.0 for spec text and Apache-2.0 for schemas/code; v1 has no provenance/permission/signing layer (third-party analysis); client support claims not independently tested

source_title: $1 million hacker challenge for Vercel Sandbox
claim_summary: Two-week HackerOne challenge (Aug 18-Sep 1) on Firecracker microVM compute and host-side network-firewall boundaries; pool up to $1M, max $50K per report; live PoC required
limitation: Findings post (1,285 reports; $242K paid; kernel zero-day and cross-tenant issues) is dated 2026-10-14, outside window, and its valid-report counts do not reconcile

source_title: The end of credential sprawl for agents
claim_summary: Vercel Connect generally available after a public beta of 100+ connectors; GA adds fine-grained RBAC, audit logs and token/trigger observability
limitation: Pricing differs from the June post FAQ: June FAQ bills Pro/Enterprise token requests at $3 per 10K token requests, while this Aug 25 page bills Pro at $3 per 1,000 token requests and $0.95 per 1,000 triggers (raw page text, 2026-10-16 spot-check); verify current pricing before use; provider-dependent revocation unchanged

source_title: Introducing Run SDK: secure eval for your agents
claim_summary: Package for running untrusted JS/TS in a fresh QuickJS context in a worker thread with only host-exposed functions; approval/auth interrupts with signed resume token; powers AI SDK code-mode tool execution
limitation: Vendor directs OS-level workloads to Sandbox; no independent escape testing; repo LICENSE Apache-2.0 (GitHub API reports NOASSERTION; file read)

source_title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Image Optimization API when AVIF files are used
claim_summary: Two critical advisories published Aug 25: AVIF image-optimization RCE (GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4) and Windows-hosted RCE (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36 / CVE-2026-75604); fixed in 15.5.24 and 16.3.3 (GitHub releases Aug 25)
limitation: Netlify states its platform did not run the affected paths; exposure is deployment-specific; links to libheif upstream fix

source_title: Reproducing, disclosing, and fixing the libheif vulnerability with Hacktron and the maintainers
claim_summary: Timeline: Hacktron reported a libheif heap overflow reachable via libvips/sharp in Next.js image optimization on Aug 11-12; Vercel platform mitigation Aug 13; Next.js release and libheif v1.23.2 on Aug 25
limitation: Upstream advisory GHSA-g89c-p67h-r497 (CVE-2026-84383, critical) confirmed via GitHub API; post does not say AI found the bug

source_title: The Vercel Bug Bounty Program is now publicly available
claim_summary: Previously private HackerOne program opened publicly, covering all Vercel platform products and open-source projects
limitation: No payout table or private-program statistics in post; program existence is not evidence of lower vulnerability rate

source_title: State of agent skills
claim_summary: Vendor reports about 1M skills and nearly 280M installs in seven months; 375 skills (0.04%) account for 62% of installs; nearly half of skills installed exactly once
feature: agent skill discovery and reuse concentration
limitation: Authors state installs are not unique people or independent choices; classified sample only; no security/quality screening of skills reported

source_title: Next.js 16.4
claim_summary: Cache Components recommended for every app and default in create-next-app; next upgrade --agent workflow; experimental agentUpgrade reminders (default policy 'security'); experimental opt-in agentFeedback drafts reviewed before sending; Cache Components to become default in Next.js 17
limitation: Blog dated Oct 6 while GitHub release v16.4.0 is Oct 7 UTC; agent-upgrade success unmeasured; Oct 14 critical advisories (outside window) followed
